explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and from October 5, 2026 it becomes a CME futures contract, so the market will show a forward curve as well as spot. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.53/hr, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve once it lists (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: $2.66/hr index (+1.1% 7d); 1-yr contract $2.35 (Mar-26) vs $1.70 (Oct-25); RunPod H100 SXM secure raised to $3.49
indicators.why: This is the marginal clearing price of installed AI compute and the most direct public read on whether capacity is being discounted; it is published daily and becomes a CME-listed futures contract on Oct 5, 2026.
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if the Silicon Data H100 index holds below ~$2.00/hr for a month, if spot trades below the one-year contract rate (inversion), or if the CME H100 curve lists in steep (>15%) backwardation; the Oct-2025 trough of $1.70 is the floor to remember.
indicators.note: Sep 15 index check: SDH100RT $2.66/GPU-hr, +1.1% over 7 days, essentially flat on the $2.67 of Aug 28 - the index has now held $2.65-2.68 for three weeks, a third above the $2.00 flip level. New companion indices: H100-hyperscaler $7.20 (+0.1%), A100 $1.58 (-1.9%), H200 $3.28 (-0.9%), B200 $5.72 (+0.4%). First list-price move of the gap: RunPod raised H100 SXM secure from $3.29 to $3.49 (+6%, page updated Sep 13) with community unchanged at $2.69; Lambda H100 SXM still $3.99-4.29. Divergence worth watching: Silicon Data's LLM token index fell to $0.97 (-1.3% 7d, proprietary-model leg -8.1%) while GPU rates held - compute input prices firm, model output prices falling. CME H100 futures list Oct 5.

indicators.name: B200 / Blackwell rental price, $/GPU-hour (on-demand)
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 index $5.72 (+0.4% 7d) vs $5.65 Aug 28; RunPod B200 $5.98/$6.79, B300 $6.94/$7.89, Lambda B200 $6.69-6.99 all unchanged; B200/H100 ratio ~2.15x
indicators.why: Blackwell is where new supply lands, so this is the first place a glut would show; if B200 rates fell toward H100 rates while Rubin ships, capacity would be outrunning demand.
indicators.watch: Bearish if tier-1 neocloud B200 on-demand drops below ~$4.50/hr, if the B200/H100 price ratio compresses below ~2x, or if lead times for 8-GPU Blackwell nodes fall to same-week availability.
indicators.note: Sep 15 price-page check: Lambda B200 SXM6 $6.69 (8x) to $6.99 (1x) unchanged since August; RunPod B200 $5.98 community / $6.79 secure and B300 $6.94 / $7.89 unchanged (only the H100 SXM secure tier was repriced, upward). Silicon Data's B200 index drifted up to $5.72 from $5.65 over the 18-day gap, keeping the B200/H100 ratio at ~2.15x - no compression toward the 2x flip level. The one soft reading is the H200 index at $3.28 (-0.9% 7d). Context unchanged: Nvidia said on the Aug 26 call that Blackwell and early Rubin supply is sold out through FY28.

indicators.name: Legacy-GPU residual value: used H100 prices, A100/H100 rates and booked useful lives
indicators.value: 2020-vintage GPUs contracted to 2029 'at full freight'; A100 index $1.58/hr, above the $1.50 trigger; MSFT 2-6 yr and Meta 5.5 yr server lives unchanged
indicators.why: Depreciation is the biggest cost in a GPU cloud; if old chips still earn money the 5-6 year accounting lives hold and no write-downs are coming, whereas collapsing used-H100 prices would be the first hard evidence of oversupply.
indicators.watch: Bearish if 8-GPU H100 servers trade below ~50% of new-build cost on the secondary market, if A100/H100 rental rates fall below ~$1.50/hr, or if any hyperscaler extends server lives beyond 6 years to flatter earnings; also watch for Hopper impairments at neoclouds.
indicators.note: The legacy rental leg is drifting but holding: Silicon Data's A100 index reads $1.58/hr on Sep 15 (-1.9% 7d, vs $1.61 in late August) with the A100-hyperscaler index flat at $3.75, still above the $1.50 bearish trigger; RunPod A100 SXM is unchanged at $1.39/$1.59 (PCIe $1.19 community) and Lambda A100 80GB at $3.99 (8x). No used-H100 price prints, impairments or useful-life changes surfaced between Aug 28 and Sep 15 - Microsoft's 2-6 year and Meta's 5.5-year schedules stand, as does CoreWeave's claim of 2020-vintage GPUs contracted to 2029 at full freight. The Economist (Sep 3) flagged neocloud depreciation as the sector's key risk, but flagged no accounting change.

indicators.name: All-in AI data-center build cost, $ per GW (with GPUs / ex-GPUs)
indicators.why: Cost per GW sets the revenue a campus must earn per GPU-hour to clear its cost of capital; rising cost means supply is constrained (good for rental prices) but raises the bar for returns and the size of the debt stack.
indicators.watch: Discounting signal if Nvidia rack ASPs or $/GW start falling (Nvidia gross margin guided below ~72%, rack prices cut) while rental $/hr does not rise; bubble-risk signal if ex-GPU cost (power, shell, turbines) keeps inflating faster than rental rates.
indicators.note: Foxconn chairman Young Liu (reported Jun 20, 2026) put a 1 GW Vera Rubin data center at up to $47B: 3,557 racks at ~$9.1M each plus roughly $15B of physical infrastructure, with a $1.3B annual power bill. Costs are still rising: Nvidia raised AI server prices ~15% on memory costs (Aug 23) and Rubin Ultra racks are estimated at $21M.

indicators.name: Server DRAM / HBM contract price momentum (QoQ) and DRAM spot
indicators.value: 2Q26 DRAM industry revenue $154.7B +59.5% QoQ; 3Q26 contracts +13-18%, 4Q26 guided +3-8%; DDR5 16Gb spot $54.33 (Sep 14) vs $53.93 (Aug 27); high-capacity NOR seen +90-110% in 2H26
indicators.why: Memory is the tightest physical input to AI servers (HBM is 25-30% of a Rubin rack) and contract prices are negotiated quarterly, so this is the earliest cyclical input to turn; a price rollover would precede GPU discounting.
indicators.watch: Bearish when server DRAM or HBM contract prices go negative QoQ (TrendForce already guides 4Q26 to only +3-8%), when 2027 HBM4 contracts are signed at lower prices, or when DRAMeXchange DDR5 spot falls >20% from peak; also watch whether CSPs start cutting memory per system, which TrendForce now flags as their cost response.
indicators.note: TrendForce's Sep 7 release puts 2Q26 DRAM industry revenue at $154.73B, +59.5% QoQ, with supplier inventories at historic lows and bits prioritised to servers (Samsung 39.4% share, +63.4% QoQ; SK hynix 24.9%, +37.9%; Micron 23.3%, +65.5%); it reiterates 3Q26 conventional contract prices moderating to +13-18% QoQ as PC/phone buyers struggle to absorb increases. A Sep 14 release adds that AI is absorbing NOR flash capacity too, with high-capacity NOR prices seen +90-110% in 2H26. Spot is drifting up, not breaking: DDR5 16Gb averaged $54.33 on Sep 14 (flat d/d, vs $53.93 on Aug 27), DDR4 16Gb $89.25 (-0.6%), NAND MLC 32Gb $18.94 (+1.6%). Next catalysts: Micron's FQ4 print Sep 30 and the 4Q26 contract round (guided to only +3-8% - the first real deceleration test); the 2027 HBM +70-140% view stands.

indicators.name: Power constraint: ERCOT interconnection queue, gas-turbine backlog and lead times
indicators.value: 474 GW ERCOT queue (~427 GW data centers) vs ~193 GW installed; first Batch Zero audit outputs: Galaxy 1.63 GW approved + 2.6 GW conditional, Cipher 3.2 GW conditional; new-DC interconnection pause holds
indicators.why: Power, not chips, is now the binding constraint on new capacity, which keeps installed GPUs scarce and rental prices firm; it also reveals how much announced demand is speculative once regulators force projects to prove financing.
indicators.watch: ERCOT files its Batch Zero eligibility-verification and community-impact reports by Dec 10, 2026 for the Dec 17 PUCT open meeting, with RFIs going out Aug-Sep and cure periods Oct-Nov: large queue withdrawals (BNEF flags 49.8 GW at risk) would show phantom demand. Turbine slot cancellations or resales, falling data-center PPA prices, or turbine prices retreating from the $600/kW 2027 forecast would signal the build is slowing.
indicators.note: The audit is now producing outputs. Galaxy said on Sep 8 that ERCOT approved Helios I and II (800 MW + 830 MW) as Batch Zero Base Load while Caspian, Selene and Helios III (2.6 GW) got conditional 'Studied Load' status subject to the system-wide study; Cipher reported conditional classifications for 3.2 GW on Sep 10 - so real projects are being validated rather than culled, but capacity allocation is now rationed by the grid operator. Gov. Abbott's freeze on new data-centre interconnections pending the energy/water audit (ordered early August) still holds, and the utilities complex wobbled on it (Sep 7 coverage of Texas 'freezing' DC demand). Demand keeps compounding regardless: Microsoft said Sep 10-11 it plans ~38 GW of data-centre capacity by 2032, tripling its compute. Turbine leg unchanged: GE Vernova 116 GW backlog, Siemens Energy 69 GW firm, 2028-30 deliveries.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capex vs cloud backlog (RPO) growth, and capex as % of cloud revenue
indicators.value: Oracle RPO $664B (+$209B y/y, only +$26B q/q) incl >$30B new AI contracts, funded by a $20B stock sale; Broadcom AI rev $16.7B +221%, Q4 guide $34.8B +93%; 2026 capex ~= $1.0T vs ~$2.4T backlog
indicators.why: Capex is the supply side and RPO is the contracted demand side; as long as backlog grows faster than capex the build is pre-sold, but capex above 100% of cloud revenue with negative free cash flow means the cycle is now funded by debt and equity and is sensitive to any demand wobble.
indicators.watch: Bearish if RPO growth decelerates below capex growth for two quarters, if 2027 capex consensus (+57% per Morgan Stanley) gets cut or 'digestion' language appears, or if backlog concentration in a few AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) produces a cancellation or renegotiation.
indicators.note: Both legs printed in the gap. Backlog: Oracle's Q1 FY27 (Sep 10) showed revenue $19.3B +30%, cloud $11.6B +62%, OCI $7.4B +121%, and RPO of $664B - up $209B y/y (~46%) with more than $30B of new AI contracts, but only +$26B q/q after last quarter's +363% y/y print, so the second derivative has turned; operating cash flow was $23B yet coverage flags free cash flow near -$24B, and Oracle completed a $20B at-the-market equity sale - the build is now visibly equity-funded. Supply: Broadcom's Q3 FY26 (Sep 2) delivered revenue of $29.6B +86% with AI semiconductor revenue tripling to $16.7B (+221% y/y, +54% q/q) and Q4 guided to ~$34.8B (+93%); call coverage says FY27 AI revenue is guided to roughly double, with Anthropic reported as its top XPU customer - a second $10B+ custom-silicon buyer at scale. Microsoft's 38 GW-by-2032 plan (Sep 10-11) keeps capex compounding. Read: still pre-sold, but Oracle is the first big backlog print to decelerate while funding shifts to equity.

indicators.name: Neocloud financing: CoreWeave loan/bond spreads, CDS, vendor backstops, customer concentration
indicators.value: No new CoreWeave debt print since the Aug 3 SOFR+550 flex; interest expense $640M/qtr (2.4x y/y); AI-related debt issuance near $500B; CoreWeave pays ~SOFR+550 vs Nebius ~+250 - a hardening two-tier market
indicators.why: Neoclouds are the levered marginal builder of GPU capacity; their cost of debt, covenants and dependence on Nvidia backstops show whether lenders still believe rental prices will cover depreciation, and they are the first place a compute-price decline turns into forced selling.
indicators.watch: Escalation if new deals price above SOFR+600 or 11% yields, CDS above 1,000bp, deals pulled or downsized, Nvidia's rent-back backstop extended to tier-1 neoclouds, or a top customer (CoreWeave's A/B/C are 36%/26%/10% of revenue) renegotiates; improvement if spreads retrace toward the April 9.75% level or if CoreWeave can tap convertible/equity-linked money on Nebius-like terms.
indicators.note: Quiet on new prints, louder on scrutiny. CoreWeave's own feed shows no new financing between Aug 28 and Sep 15 (September items were DARPA and physical-AI announcements); the gap-period news was analytical - interest expense hit $640M last quarter, 2.4x a year earlier (Motley Fool, Sep 1), The Economist sized up neocloud leverage (Sep 3, 'bigger - and riskier'), and Bloomberg (via Yahoo, Sep 14) counts AI-related debt sales near $500B while contrasting CoreWeave's ~SOFR+550 cost with Nebius at roughly +250 - the two-tier market between anchor-tenant balance sheets and merchant neoclouds is hardening, not healing. Goldman was sounding out investors for a $1.15B CoreWeave-tied data-centre bond (Bloomberg, Aug 19). Nebius's September news was commercial, not debt (Palantir sovereign-AI partnership, Sep 8). A reported GSAM-led $6.6B GPU-backed OpenAI-related financing (Aug 27) could not be verified on this pass. AMD reportedly extended a $300M loan backstop to Crusoe (resurfaced Sep 12), extending the vendor-financing pattern beyond Nvidia.

indicators.name: Nvidia data-center revenue growth, gross margin and customer concentration
indicators.value: DC rev $89.0B +117% YoY (Q2 FY27), GM 75.0%, Q3 guide $108B at 74%; 10-Q: one direct customer >=10% of Q2 revenue (16%) vs two a year ago (23%+16%); five customers = 70% of receivables; supply commitments $279B
indicators.why: Nvidia's margin is the purest read on whether GPUs are being discounted at the source, and its concentration plus growing vendor-financing (backstops, campus guarantees) shows how much of demand is circular.
indicators.watch: Bearish if gross margin is guided below ~72% for more than one quarter, data-center revenue grows <5% sequentially, three-customer concentration exceeds 60% in the 10-Q, DSO climbs past 60 days, or backstop commitments expand beyond the $108.5B disclosed; Q3 FY27 report due ~Nov 2026.
indicators.note: The Q2 FY27 10-Q (filed Aug 26) settles the concentration question the last note left open, and it improved: only one direct customer crossed 10% of quarterly revenue, at 16%, versus two (23% and 16%) in the year-ago quarter, and the first half has three at 16%, 15% and 13% (44% combined) - revenue concentration is broadening as neoclouds, sovereigns and a second custom-silicon ecosystem scale, well below the 60% flip level. The stress shows up on the balance sheet instead: five direct customers now account for 22%, 14%, 13%, 11% and 10% of accounts receivable (70%), up from three at 25/18/13% in January, consistent with DSO stretching to 60 days - Nvidia is financing buyers through payment terms as well as equity stakes ('its customers' credit line', as Sep 13 coverage put it). Supply commitments of $279B, the 71-72% Q4 margin trough on memory costs and zero-China guidance are unchanged; Broadcom's Sep 2 print (AI revenue +221%) confirms the custom-XPU bid is additive rather than substitutive so far. Next print ~Nov.
